h: Cromwell's Town and the Great Ouse Valley
p: Huntingdon wears its history lightly, but there's a lot of it. The Cromwell Museum sits in the old grammar school building where both Oliver Cromwell and Samuel Pepys were pupils, and it holds a fascinating collection of Cromwell's belongings and portraits. It's small enough to suit children with short attention spans.

On the edge of town, Hinchingbrooke Country Park has woodland, meadows and lakes, with easy trails and a play area, great for a run-around after a few hours in the car. A few miles east, St Ives is a lovely riverside market town, famous for its medieval bridge with a little chapel built into the middle of it, one of only a handful of bridge chapels left in England.

To the south-west of Hamerton, Grafham Water is a big reservoir with cycling and walking routes around its shore, sailing, and wildlife hides. It's a great place for a bike ride, with a circuit that's long enough to tire teenagers out and flat enough for younger riders on the shorter sections.

At the zoo, plan for plenty of time on your feet. The site is spread across open countryside, and some of the rarer species are shy, so patient visitors get the best sightings. Bring a packed lunch and a waterproof, as the flat fenland breeze can be chilly even on bright days. Peterborough, with its splendid cathedral, is also within easy reach up the A1. It's a rewarding, unhurried day.
